summary: The oldest surviving lookout of its design in California, built 1931 on Shasta-Trinity NF, staffed until 1981, restored in 1997 and rentable since 1998.

facts.design: L-4 cab, 14'x14' with catwalk, atop an enclosed tapered 13-foot wooden tower, a 1917 design said to be unique to the California region
facts.status_note: No longer used for active fire detection; restored and operated as a rental cabin.

access.note: Forest Service rental; reached by steep, narrow dirt roads through private timberland with active log-truck traffic; gate combination must be requested a week ahead by phone.

visit.trail_note: High-clearance vehicle recommended; hiking north 3 miles reaches the Pacific Crest Trail.

events.note: Built as an L-4 cab atop an enclosed, tapered wooden tower, a 1917-era design.
Used by the Forest Service on a regular basis until 1981.
Restored to its original specifications/character by the Forest Service and volunteers.
Placed on the lookout rental program.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, May 15, 1998 (per brief/NHLR record).

evidence.supports: Built 1931; L-4 cab on enclosed tapered 13-foot tower, 1917 design unique to California; oldest of its type remaining; restored 1997; rental program 1998.
evidence.quote: Built in 1931, Girard Ridge Fire Lookout is a 14' x 14' L-4 cab with catwalk atop an enclosed tapered 13' wooden tower, a 1917 design unique to the California region. It is the oldest structure of its type remaining in the state.

evidence.supports: Restoration and rental program entry dates.
evidence.quote: No longer active for detection on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, it was restored to its original specifications in 1997 by the Forest Service and volunteers... it was placed on the lookout rental program in 1998.

evidence.supports: Built 1931, used regularly until 1981, restored 1997, oldest of its design in CA.
evidence.quote: Girard Ridge Lookout was constructed in 1931 and used by the Forest Service on a regular basis until 1981... The structure at Girard Ridge is reportedly the oldest lookout of its particular design remaining in California. It was restored to its original character in 1997.

evidence.supports: Access road conditions, gate combination process, cabin amenities and cooking restrictions, and the views from the cab.
evidence.quote: The dirt roads leading to Girard Ridge Lookout are at times steep and narrow; high clearance vehicles are recommended. The access roads to the lookout run primarily through private timberlands and log truck traffic should be expected.

evidence.supports: Cabin interior details and fuel/fire restrictions.
evidence.quote: The use of portable stoves using gas, jellied petroleum or pressurized liquid fuel is allowed with a valid California campfire permit, but no wood or charcoal fires are permitted.

sources.title: Girard Ridge Lookout, Shasta-Trinity National Forest
